problem: Existing EQA tasks name the target object explicitly, so agents cannot use external knowledge (e.g. 'knife is used for cutting food'), lack logical reasoning over multiple objects (and/or), and have no memory across multiple questions in the same environment.
motivation: Realistic household questions require commonsense knowledge, multi-object logic and repeated questioning in the same room. A persistent structured memory (3D scene graph) plus a knowledge graph would allow joint reasoning, avoid re-exploration and let multiple agents cooperate.
key_idea: Translate the question with a neural text-to-SQL synthesizer into programs that run over a 3D scene graph built online and over ConceptNet knowledge, both to pick relevant regions to explore (MCTS scan executor) and to answer.
insight: The SQL planner cuts path length about half versus full scan (Ours+FS 131.1 vs Ours 82.7) at roughly 1% accuracy cost. Baselines without the KG (w/o KG 31.8%) perform about like blind/prior (31.9/30.4), so the knowledge is necessary. With GT scene graph accuracy reaches 90.3%, so the program synthesis is sound and the bottleneck is perception (Mask R-CNN and voxel clustering, GT Segm reaches 67.5%).
method: Scene graph state memory: Mask R-CNN segmentation back-projected with depth into semantic voxels; same-category voxels within a threshold are connected into 3D objects, with Contain/In/On/Holding, Above/Below and Near relations (0.25 m thresholds).
Question Answerer: attentional seq2seq (Bahdanau) text-to-SQL trained on synthetic grammar-generated questions; SQL executed in PostgreSQL over tables built from the scene graph and ConceptNet KG.

Action Planner: a second text-to-SQL program queries scene priors (from the train set) plus KG to return plausible object relation triplets; voxels in regions where the target cannot appear are removed.

MCTS scan executor: finds a shortest viewport sequence (x,y,azimuth,inclination) covering relevant voxels; node value 1-(l-lmin)/(lmax-lmin); multi-agent supported by agents choosing viewports in turn.

K-EQA dataset: AI2-THOR, 6000 rooms, 60k questions (Existence/Counting/Comparing/Enumerating) generated from a formal grammar with ConceptNet (7,451 triplets) and scene relations; K-EQA Extension adds and/or logic; tag and sub-tag balancing removes answer bias.
Multi-turn and multi-agent: the persistent scene graph memory reused across 10 questions and shared among agents to reduce path length.

setting.backbone: Mask R-CNN + attentional LSTM seq2seq text-to-SQL (trained), PostgreSQL executor, MCTS planner
setting.training_data: K-EQA train split: 50k synthetic questions with SQL programs; Mask R-CNN trained on AI2-THOR; scene priors from train set
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with camera pose (voxel reconstruction)
setting.action_space: low-level Move/Rotate, planned via viewport sequences
setting.privileged: none for main method (GT segmentation / GT scene graph only in oracle ablations); ConceptNet used as external knowledge

numbers_note: Own benchmark (K-EQA); no standard benchmark reported. Multi-agent (5 agents: 40.4% acc, length 35.6, speedup 2.32) and multi-turn (10 turns: 42.7%, length 12.5, speedup 6.64) results also given.
results: On K-EQA the method reaches 41.3% overall accuracy vs 31.9% Blindfold, 30.4% Priori and 31.8% w/o KG, and performs worse on the K-EQA Extension (37.1%). Multi-turn memory cuts per-question path length from 82.7 to 12.5 at 10 turns with accuracy stable, and 5 agents give 2.32x speedup.
limitations: Accuracy is low (41.3%), especially for counting/enumerating, limited by Mask R-CNN and voxel clustering that miscount small objects
Evaluated only on the authors' synthetic template-generated questions in AI2-THOR; no real robot or standard benchmarks
Text-to-SQL trained on grammar-synthetic questions may not generalize to natural free-form language; no interaction with objects
